# Results

Writing outline: Results

1. Organize Results around monitoring coverage, environmental surfaces, oyster occurrences and background, MaxEnt selection and validation, fitted responses, predicted suitability, and HSI agreement. Reserve ecological explanations and management implications for Discussion.
   - Use the saved water-quality summaries, IPDW validation results, four-partition ENMeval/maxnet exports, and aligned rasters for numerical results. The older five-fold dismo outputs describe a different model.

```{r}
#| label: results-setup
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
library(sf)
library(raster)
library(ipdw)
library(patchwork)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(scales)

# Raw water-quality data
chla_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "chla_raw.rds"))
do_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "do.rds"))
sal_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "salinity_raw.rds"))
turb_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "turb_raw.rds"))
water_temp_raw <- readRDS(here("2-data", "raw", "water_temp_raw.rds"))

raw_data <- list(
  "Chlorophyll-a" = chla_raw,
  "Dissolved Oxygen" = do_raw,
  "Salinity" = sal_raw,
  "Turbidity" = turb_raw,
  "Temperature" = water_temp_raw
)

# Processed water-quality data
chla_proc <- readRDS(here("2-data", "processed", "proc_chla.rds"))
do_proc <- readRDS(here("2-data", "processed", "proc_do.rds"))
sal_proc <- readRDS(here("2-data", "processed", "proc_sal.rds"))
turb_proc <- readRDS(here("2-data", "processed", "proc_turb.rds"))
water_temp_proc <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "processed", "proc_water_temp.rds")
)

processed_data <- list(
  "Chlorophyll-a" = chla_proc,
  "Dissolved Oxygen" = do_proc,
  "Salinity" = sal_proc,
  "Turbidity" = turb_proc,
  "Temperature" = water_temp_proc
)

parameter_units <- c(
  "Chlorophyll-a" = "ug/L",
  "Dissolved Oxygen" = "mg/L",
  "Salinity" = "ppt",
  "Turbidity" = "NTU",
  "Temperature" = "degrees C"
)

# Saved IPDW sensitivity results
sensitivity_results <- list(
  "Dissolved Oxygen" = readRDS(
    here("2-data", "models", "sensitivity_test_do.rds")
  ),
  "Salinity" = readRDS(
    here("2-data", "models", "sensitivity_test_sal.rds")
  ),
  "Turbidity" = readRDS(
    here("2-data", "models", "sensitivity_test_turb.rds")
  ),
  "Temperature" = readRDS(
    here("2-data", "models", "sensitivity_test_water_temp.rds")
  )
)

# Saved final IPDW validation results
model_stats <- list(
  "Dissolved Oxygen" = readRDS(
    here("2-data", "models", "stats_do.rds")
  ),
  "Salinity" = readRDS(
    here("2-data", "models", "stats_sal.rds")
  ),
  "Turbidity" = readRDS(
    here("2-data", "models", "stats_turb.rds")
  ),
  "Temperature" = readRDS(
    here("2-data", "models", "stats_water_temp.rds")
  )
)

# Saved final environmental rasters
raster_results <- list(
  "Dissolved Oxygen" = raster(
    here("2-data", "rasters", "rast_do.tif")
  ),
  "Salinity" = raster(
    here("2-data", "rasters", "rast_sal.tif")
  ),
  "Turbidity" = raster(
    here("2-data", "rasters", "rast_turb.tif")
  ),
  "Temperature" = raster(
    here("2-data", "rasters", "rast_wTemp.tif")
  )
)

study_area <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "processed", "study_area.rds")
)

oyster_points <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "processed", "proc_oys_reefs.rds")
)
```

## Water-Quality Data Coverage


<!--
Writing outline: Water-Quality Data Coverage

1. Start with 25,665 raw parameter records across 174 distinct station identifiers. The raw datasets span January 2005 through December 2024. Warm-season processing retained 11,946 observations (46.5%). Use @tbl-data-summary for the breakdown.
   - Chlorophyll-a: 1,847 raw observations at 54 stations, 666 retained observations, 25 finite means across 27 bin rows.
   - Dissolved oxygen: 6,261 at 169 stations, 3,010 retained, 68 of 68 finite. Salinity: 6,994 at 159 stations, 3,400 retained, 67 of 67 finite.
   - Turbidity: 3,402 at 146 stations, 1,429 retained, 58 of 61 finite. Temperature: 7,161 at 169 stations, 3,441 retained, 68 of 68 finite.
   - The 291 parameter-specific bin rows contain 286 finite means and represent 71 distinct bin IDs. The table's processed station counts are station groups within bins. They include some groups with no usable observations after screening.
2. Describe the concentration of stations in Escambia and Pensacola Bays and the gaps farther east. Chlorophyll-a had especially sparse eastern coverage and was excluded before predictor interpolation for the final model. Use @fig-monitoring-coverage.
-->



There were 25,665 raw observations from across all five parameter datasets, representing 174 unique site locations. Chlorophyll-a had 1,845 records from 54 sites. Processing resulted in 27 binned values using 666. Dissolved Oxygen had 6,261 observations from 169 sites. Processing reduced the data to 68 binned values using 3,010 observations. Salinity returned 6,994 observation values from 159 sites. The data was processed into 67 binned values using 3,400 observations.  Turbidity had 3,402 observed values from 146 sites. After processing there were 61 binned values using 1,429 observations. Water temperature had 7,161 raw observations from 169 sites. Data processing returned 68 binned values using 3,441 observations. Overall, data processing returned 291 parameterized data values using 11,946 fo the 25,665 original values, representing 46.5% of the original dataset (@tbl-data-summary).

For all parameters, the data was heavily skewed spatially, with the majority of samples located in Escambia and Pensacola Bays. Chlorophyll-a in particular had much fewer sites and almost no observations located in the eastern half of the study area. Due to such a lack of spatial distribution, chlorophyll-a was subsequently dropped from the analysis (@fig-monitoring-coverage). 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of raw and processed warm-season water-quality data by environmental parameter."
#| echo: true
#| warning: false

wq_summary <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Parameter,      ~`Raw observations`, ~`Raw stations`, ~`Retained observations`, ~`Retained stations`, ~`Spatial bins`,
  "Chlorophyll-a", 1847,                54,              666,                      48,                   27,
  "Dissolved Oxygen",            6261,                169,             3010,                     145,                  68,
  "Salinity",      6994,                159,             3400,                     135,                  67,
  "Turbidity",     3402,                146,             1429,                     122,                  61,
  "Temperature",   7161,                169,             3441,                     145,                  68
)

knitr::kable(
  wq_summary,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
  digits = 0,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-monitoring-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Spatial distribution of monitoring stations represented in each raw water-quality dataset."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

monitoring_sites <- imap_dfr(
  raw_data,
  \(data, parameter) {
    data %>%
      dplyr::select(Location_Identifier, geometry) %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(Location_Identifier)) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(Location_Identifier) %>%
      dplyr::slice(1) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(parameter = parameter)
  }
) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(study_area))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = study_area,
    fill = "grey95",
    color = "grey45",
    linewidth = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = monitoring_sites,
    color = "#2166AC",
    size = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## Environmental Predictor Results


<!--
Writing outline: Environmental Predictor Results

1. Summarize the four water-quality sensitivity analyses.
   - Each used 36 settings, with nine distance powers from 0.25 to 3.00 and ranges of 5, 10, 15, and 20 km, evaluated across five independently seeded five-fold spatial partitions. All four final surfaces used power 0.25 and a 10 km maximum range. Cite @fig-ipdw-sensitivity for the candidate settings and @tbl-ipdw-validation for repeated validation at the settings used.
   - In the validation table, SD measures variation across spatial partitions, signed bias is predicted minus observed, and coverage refers to usable observed and predicted pairs. Compare errors within each parameter's measurement units.
2. Add oyster recruitment as a separate fitted predictor result.
   - Ten source estimates range from 0 to 14.76. The saved validation used power 0.25 and a 10 km range and reports MAE 5.510, RMSE 6.481, mean bias -0.808, and 10 of 10 usable pairs. These are from a separate validation summary. Confirm its fold design and the recruitment units before describing it alongside repeated water-quality validation.
   - The recruitment surface has 33,323 finite 100 m cells, with range 0 to 14.76, mean 7.354, and SD 3.035. The processed input and shapefile identify the recruitment value field but leave its units unspecified. Use stats_oys_rec.rds and rast_oys_rec.tif for the saved results.
   - List categorical sediment alongside recruitment and the four water-quality rasters when describing the six fitted predictors. Sediment categories in Methods are mud, muddy sand, and sand.
-->



Each parameter (save for chlorophyll-a) was interpolated into predicted surface rasters using an inverse-path distance weighting algorithm. To ensure the highest accuracy was achieved, a sensitivy analysis was conducted on each parameter model using 36 distance-power/range combinations, which were in turn evaluated across five random five-fold spatial partitions. Powers ranged from 0.25 to 3.00, and  maximum range values evaluated were 5, 10, 15, and 20 km (@fig-ipdw-sensitivity). 

While the results of every sensitivity analysis will be reported here, it should be noted that after running all parameters it was decided that a distance power of 0.25 and a max range of 10km was to be used. This decision was made as there was little variation in results of the sensitivity analysis and a smoother prediction surface was preferred to better represent the smoother gradients found in the real world. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-ipdw-sensitivity
#| fig-cap: "Mean MAE across distance-power and maximum-range combinations evaluated using repeated five-fold spatial cross-validation. Red outlines identify the parameter combinations used for the final interpolation models."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

plot_sensitivity <- function(result, stats, parameter) {
  power_levels <- sort(unique(result$summary$dist_power))
  range_levels <- sort(unique(result$summary$max_range))

  plot_data <- result$summary %>%
    mutate(
      dist_power = factor(dist_power, levels = power_levels),
      max_range = factor(max_range, levels = range_levels)
    )

  selected_data <- result$summary %>%
    filter(
      near(dist_power, stats$dist_power[[1]]),
      max_range == stats$max_range[[1]]
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      dist_power = factor(dist_power, levels = power_levels),
      max_range = factor(max_range, levels = range_levels)
    )

  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = dist_power,
      y = max_range,
      fill = mean_MAE
    )
  ) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_tile(
      data = selected_data,
      fill = NA,
      color = "red",
      linewidth = 1.2
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_MAE),
        color = mean_MAE > median(mean_MAE, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      size = 3
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      direction = -1,
      name = "Mean MAE"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("FALSE" = "black", "TRUE" = "white"),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = parameter,
      x = "Distance power",
      y = "Maximum range (m)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
}

sensitivity_plots <- imap(
  sensitivity_results,
  \(result, parameter) {
    plot_sensitivity(
      result = result,
      stats = model_stats[[parameter]],
      parameter = parameter
    )
  }
)

wrap_plots(sensitivity_plots, ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "IPDW Parameter Sensitivity Analysis",
    subtitle = "Repeated five-fold spatial cross-validation"
  )
```

### Dissolved Oxygen

<!--
Writing outline: Dissolved Oxygen

1. Report a sensitivity MAE range of 0.426 to 0.507 mg/L. The minimum was 0.426 mg/L at power 0.75 and a 10 km range, with 100% coverage. Use @fig-ipdw-sensitivity.
2. At the selected power 0.25 and 10 km range, report mean MAE 0.431 (SD 0.006), RMSE 0.552 (SD 0.004), mean bias +0.013 mg/L, and 100% coverage. Use @tbl-ipdw-validation.
3. Describe the 33,792 finite cells, with range 5.28 to 7.99 mg/L, mean 6.52, and SD 0.26. Check the direction of the gradient and the locations of the lowest values against @fig-environmental-rasters before describing them in prose.
-->


Dissolved oxygen sensitivity had a mean MAE ranging from 0.426 to 0.507 mg/L. The lowest mean MAE with 100% prediction was 0.425mg/L using a distance power of 0.75 and max range of 10km (@tbl-ipdw-validation). The predicted rater surface values ranged from 5.28mg/L to 7.99mg/L (n = 33,792; µ = 6.52; σ = 0.26; @tbl-raster-summary). The final prediction model achieved 100% coverage with a MAE of 0.431 mg/L (σ = 0.006) with RMSE = 0.552 mg/L (σ = 0.004). The model tended to over predict by +0.013 mg/L. Spatially, dissolved oxygen generally decreased in the western portions of the study area. With the lowest values appearing in East Bay and northern Blackwater Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters).   


### Salinity

<!--
Writing outline: Salinity

1. Report a sensitivity MAE range of 2.397 to 3.125 ppt. The overall minimum was 2.397 ppt at power 3.00 and a 5 km range, with mean coverage of 96.1%. The best full-coverage setting was power 0.50 at 10 km, with MAE 2.489983 ppt. The selected 0.25 and 10 km setting had MAE 2.490102 ppt, about 0.000120 ppt higher than the best full-coverage setting. Use @fig-ipdw-sensitivity.
2. At the selected setting, report mean MAE 2.490 (SD 0.036), RMSE 3.444 (SD 0.024), mean bias +0.140 ppt, and 100% coverage. Use @tbl-ipdw-validation.
3. Describe the 33,792 finite cells, with range 2.31 to 26.73 ppt, mean 16.36, and SD 3.14. The map shows broadly higher values in southwestern Pensacola Bay and lower values toward northern Blackwater Bay. Use @fig-environmental-rasters.
-->


The salinity sensitivity analysis had a mean MAE ranging from 2.397 ppt to 3.125 ppt. The lowest reported MAE with 100% model coverage was 2.49 ppt using distance power 0.50 and max range of 10km. The absolute lowest mean MAE was 2.397 ppt was achieved using distance power of 3.00 and a max range of 5km , but model coverage fell to 96.1%. The difference in mean MAE between the lowest achieved DP-MR combination and the actual DP-MR combination used was 0.000119 ppt (@tbl-ipdw-validation). Spatial cross-validation of the final model fit had a MAE of 2.49 ppt (σ = 0.036) and RMSE 3.444 ppt (σ = 0.024). The model slightly over predicted salinity values (+0.140 ppt) and achieved 100% coverage. The predicted values ranged from 2.31 to 26.73 ppt (n = 33,792; µ = 16.36 ppt; σ = 3.14; @tbl-raster-summary). Spatially, salinity generally decreased from west to east with the lowest values being in the northern Blackwater Bay and the highest values located in the southwestern region of Pensacola Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters). 

### Turbidity


<!--
Writing outline: Turbidity

1. Report a sensitivity MAE range of 0.696 to 0.847 NTU. The minimum was 0.696 NTU at power 1.00 and a 15 km range, with 95.1% coverage. Use @fig-ipdw-sensitivity.
2. At the selected power 0.25 and 10 km range, report mean MAE 0.745 (SD 0.018), RMSE 0.937 (SD 0.026), mean bias -0.010 NTU, and 95.1% coverage. Three of 61 bin rows had nonfinite observed means after screening, leaving 58 usable pairs. Use @tbl-ipdw-validation.
3. Describe the 33,790 finite cells, with range 0.03 to 5.23 NTU, mean 2.23, and SD 0.47. Use the mapped north-to-south contrast and check any more precise river-mouth statements against @fig-environmental-rasters.
-->



The sensitivity analysis for turbidity reported a mean MAE range from 0.696 to 0.847 NTU. The lowest mean MAE was 0.696 NTU (DP = 1.00, MR = 15km) with 95.1% model coverage (@tbl-ipdw-validation). The final model fit produced a MAE = 0.745 NTU (σ = 0.018) with RMSE = 0.937 NTU (σ = 0.026). Overall the model slightly under predicted by -0.010 NTU and achieved 95.1% coverage. The final predicted surface values ranged from 0.03 NTU to 5.23 NTU (n = 33,790; µ = 2.23 NTU; σ = 0.47; @tbl-raster-summary). Spatially, turbidity generally decreased from north to south, with the highest values occuring near the mouth of Escambia River and the lowest values occuring in the southwestern portion of Pensacola Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters).

### Water Temperature


<!--
Writing outline: Water Temperature

1. Report a sensitivity MAE range of 0.978 to 1.135 degrees C. The minimum was 0.978 degrees C at power 0.75 and a 10 km range, with 100% coverage. Use @fig-ipdw-sensitivity.
2. At the selected power 0.25 and 10 km range, report mean MAE 0.988 (SD 0.015), RMSE 1.163 (SD 0.014), mean bias -0.063 degrees C, and 100% coverage. Use @tbl-ipdw-validation.
3. Describe the 33,792 finite cells, with range 25.93 to 30.43 degrees C, mean 27.66, and SD 0.41. Use @fig-environmental-rasters for the cooler eastern and northeastern areas. These surfaces summarize long-term warm-season conditions.

Mean MAE for the water temperature sensitivity analysis ranged from 0.978 to 1.135 degrees C. The lowest mean MAE was 0.978 degrees C with 100% model coverage (DP = 0.75, MR = 10km; @tbl-ipdw-validation). The final model had a MAE of 0.988 degrees C (σ = 0.015) and RMSE was 1.163 degrees C (σ = 0.014). The model generally under predicted water temperature by -0.063 degrees C with 100% model coverage. The resulting prediction surface ranged from 25.93 to 30.43 degrees C (n = 33,792; µ = 27.66°C; σ = 0.41°C; @tbl-raster-summary). Water temperature was generally lower in the eastern portions of the study area, with the coolest values trending toward Blackwater Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ipdw-validation
#| tbl-cap: "Selected IPDW parameters and repeated spatial cross-validation performance. Values in parentheses are standard deviations across random spatial partitions."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

validation_summary <- imap_dfr(
  model_stats,
  \(stats, parameter) {
    selected_power <- stats$dist_power[[1]]
    selected_range <- stats$max_range[[1]]

    repeated_results <- sensitivity_results[[parameter]]$summary %>%
      filter(
        near(dist_power, selected_power),
        max_range == selected_range
      ) %>%
      slice(1)

    tibble(
      Parameter = parameter,
      Units = parameter_units[[parameter]],
      `Distance power` = selected_power,
      `Maximum range (km)` = selected_range / 1000,
      `Mean MAE (SD)` = sprintf(
        "%.3f (%.3f)",
        repeated_results$mean_MAE,
        repeated_results$sd_MAE
      ),
      `Mean RMSE (SD)` = sprintf(
        "%.3f (%.3f)",
        repeated_results$mean_RMSE,
        repeated_results$sd_RMSE
      ),
      `Mean bias` = sprintf(
        "%.3f",
        repeated_results$mean_Bias
      ),
      `Mean coverage` = scales::percent(
        repeated_results$mean_coverage,
        accuracy = 0.1
      )
    )
  }
)

kable(
  validation_summary,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

<!-- ## Oyster Occurrence and Background Data -->


<!--
Writing outline: Oyster Occurrence and Background Data

1. Describe how 443 processed mapped reef records became 35 after 1 km thinning (seed 42), then 34 after removing one record with incomplete predictor coverage. Raster-cell deduplication removed zero additional presences.
2. Report 34 modeled presences and 10,000 background points sampled from other cells with complete coverage of the six predictors. Background points represent available environmental conditions [@Phillips2009; @Elith2011].
   - @fig-oyster-occurrences now uses occurrence_comparison.png, with a panel for the full input set and a second panel for the processed presences and background points. Use this figure for the before-and-after comparison. Use a separate plot if showing partition assignments.
3. Report held-out presence counts of 9, 8, 9, and 8 and background counts of 5,706, 432, 2,594, and 1,268 across the four ENMeval geographic partitions. Use maxent_cross_validation_metrics.csv.
-->

Initial oyster presence data was heavily skewed and had to be thinned in order to avoid spatial bias in the model. The thinning process removed 408 of 443 records leaving 35 oyster reefs that had a minimum seperation distance of 1km. 1 additional oyster point was dropped due to lack of predictor coverage. The final model had 34 presences and 10,000 background points [@fig-oyster-occurrences]. The spatial partition held-out presence counts were well spit with values of 9, 8, 9, and 8. Background counts were less evenly split, with counts of 5,706, 432, 2,594, and 1,268, respectively. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

tmap::tmap_mode("plot")

# Combine datasets for faceting
original_pts <- oyster_points %>%
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(pb)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Panel = "A. Original Occurrences",
    Point_Type = "Presence"
  )

processed_pts <- pb %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Panel = "B. Processed Occurrences",
    Point_Type = dplyr::if_else(
      as.character(pb) == "1",
      "Presence",
      "Background"
    )
  )

plot_points <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  original_pts,
  processed_pts
)

# Establish consistent factor ordering
plot_points$Panel <- factor(
  plot_points$Panel,
  levels = c(
    "A. Original Occurrences",
    "B. Processed Occurrences"
  )
)

plot_points$Point_Type <- factor(
  plot_points$Point_Type,
  levels = c("Background", "Presence")
)

# Tight bounding box around both datasets
my_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(plot_points)

# Only 3% padding
xpad <- (my_bbox["xmax"] - my_bbox["xmin"]) * 0.03
ypad <- (my_bbox["ymax"] - my_bbox["ymin"]) * 0.03

my_bbox["xmin"] <- my_bbox["xmin"] - xpad
my_bbox["xmax"] <- my_bbox["xmax"] + xpad
my_bbox["ymin"] <- my_bbox["ymin"] - ypad
my_bbox["ymax"] <- my_bbox["ymax"] + ypad

# Single faceted map
oyster_comparison <-
  tmap::tm_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") +
  tmap::tm_shape(plot_points, bbox = my_bbox) +
  tmap::tm_dots(
    fill = "Point_Type",
    fill.scale = tmap::tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c("#B0B0B0", "#B2182B")
    ),
    fill.free = FALSE,
    size = "Point_Type",
    size.scale = tmap::tm_scale_categorical(
      values = c(0.035, 0.20)
    ),
    size.legend = tmap::tm_legend_hide(),
    plot.order = tmap::tm_plot_order(
      "fill", reverse = FALSE
    ),
    fill.legend = tmap::tm_legend(
      title = "Point Type",
      position = tmap::tm_pos_out(
        "center", "bottom"
      ),
      orientation = "landscape"
    )
  ) +
  tmap::tm_facets_wrap(
    by = "Panel",
    ncol = 2,
    free.coords = FALSE
  ) +
  tmap::tm_layout(
    asp = 0,
    frame = FALSE,
    inner.margins = 0.01,
    outer.margins = 0.01,
    panel.label.size = 1.1,
    panel.label.fontface = 2
  )

oyster_comparison

tmap_save(oyster_comparison, here::here("4-tables-and-figures", "maps", "occurrence_comparison.png"))
```

## MaxEnt Model Tuning and Selection

Overall, the models performed moderately at best with 16 of the 24 candidate models having $\bar{AUC} \le 0.50$. Across the 24 candidate models, training AUC ranged from 0.747 to 0.863, while mean validation AUC ranged from 0.460 to 0.703. Mean validation Continuous Boyce Index (CBI) ranged from −0.353 to 0.334, and mean 10th-percentile omission rates ranged from 0.115 to 0.250. AICc values ranged from 677.70 to 693.66, with model complexity ranging from 3 to 14 nonzero coefficients.

The selected model used linear, quadratic, and hinge (LQH) features with a regularization multiplier of 0.5 [@tbl-maxent-selection]. This configuration achieved the highest mean validation AUC (0.703 ± 0.136 SD) and tied for the lowest mean 10th-percentile omission rate (0.115 ± 0.091 SD). Its mean validation CBI was 0.093 ± 0.525 SD, with a training AUC of 0.862.

LQHP with a regularization multiplier of 0.5 achieved the same mean omission rate (0.115), with a slightly lower mean validation AUC (0.697) and CBI (0.046). The highest validation CBI (0.334) occurred with LQHP at a regularization multiplier of 1.0.

The lowest AICc (677.70) was achieved by the LQ configuration with a regularization multiplier of 0.5. This model had a mean validation AUC of 0.520 and CBI of −0.253, compared with 0.703 and 0.093, respectively, for the selected LQH model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-maxent-selection
#| tbl-cap: "Performance of the leading candidate MaxEnt configurations."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: true

maxent_tuning <- read.csv(
  here("4-tables-and-figures", "tables", "maxent_tuning_results.csv")
)

maxent_tuning_table <- maxent_tuning %>%
  arrange(or.10p.avg, desc(cbi.val.avg)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  transmute(
    `Feature Class` = fc,
    `Regularization Multiplier` = rm,
    `Validation AUC (Mean)` = sprintf("%.3f", auc.val.avg),
    `Validation AUC (s.d.)` = sprintf("%.3f", auc.val.sd),
    `Omission Rate (Mean)` = sprintf("%.3f", or.10p.avg),
    `Omission Rate (s.d.)` = sprintf("%.3f", or.10p.sd),
    `Validation CBI (Mean)` = sprintf("%.3f", cbi.val.avg),
    `Validation CBI (s.d.)` = sprintf("%.3f", cbi.val.sd),
    `Delta AICc` = sprintf("%.2f", delta.AICc)
  )

kable(
  maxent_tuning_table,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r","r","r","r", "c")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-variable-importance
#| fig-cap: "Relative contribution and permutation importance of environmental predictors in the selected MaxEnt model."

variable_importance <- readRDS(

)

importance_long <- variable_importance %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(contribution, permutation_importance),
    names_to = "metric",

  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      contribution = "Contribution",
      permutation_importance = "Permutation importance"
    ),
    variable = fct_reorder(variable, importance, .fun = max)
  )

ggplot(
  importance_long,

    y = variable,
    fill = metric
  )
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2166AC", "#B2182B")) +
  labs(
    x = "Importance (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## Comparison with the Existing HSI -->

<!--
Writing outline: Comparison with the Existing HSI

1. State the comparison domain and settings. Reproducing 3-scripts/5-hsi-comparison.qmd aligns the saved MaxEnt and normalized HSI rasters to complete_mask.tif with bilinear resampling. There are 31,774 paired 100 m cells (317.74 square km), 681 fewer than the full MaxEnt raster.
   - Compare the saved logistic MaxEnt surface with the normalized HSI using shared class breaks of 0, 0.20, 0.40, 0.60, 0.80, and 1. The breaks define the same numerical intervals for both scores. Their ecological interpretations depend on each model's scale [@Geselbracht2024; @Elith2011].
2. Report exact agreement in 8,750 cells (27.54%) and agreement within one class, including exact matches, in 23,315 cells (73.38%). HSI class was higher in 17,911 cells (56.37%) and MaxEnt class in 5,113 (16.09%). Continuous Spearman rho was 0.273 across the aligned surfaces. Use these metrics for descriptive model agreement [@Johnson2005].
3. Use HSI class minus MaxEnt class for the difference map, where positive values indicate higher HSI, negative values indicate higher MaxEnt, and zero indicates exact class agreement. The disabled Results comparison chunks still use placeholder inputs and a continuous difference in the opposite direction. Align the table, figure, and captions to the reproduced comparison before describing geographic patterns.
-->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-hsi-comparison
#| tbl-cap: "Cell-level comparison between MaxEnt and HSI habitat-suitability predictions."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

maxent_suitability <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "maxent_suitability.rds")
)

hsi_suitability <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "hsi_suitability.rds")
)

compareRaster(
  maxent_suitability,
  hsi_suitability,
  extent = TRUE,
  rowcol = TRUE,
  crs = TRUE,
  res = TRUE,
  orig = TRUE,
  stopiffalse = TRUE
)

comparison_data <- tibble(
  maxent = getValues(maxent_suitability),
  hsi = getValues(hsi_suitability)
) %>%
  drop_na()

hsi_comparison <- tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Pearson correlation",
    "Spearman correlation",
    "Mean signed difference",
    "Mean absolute difference",
    "Root mean square difference",
    "Cells within 0.10 suitability units"
  ),
  Value = c(
    sprintf("%.3f", cor(comparison_data$maxent, comparison_data$hsi)),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      cor(
        comparison_data$maxent,
        comparison_data$hsi,
        method = "spearman"
      )
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      mean(comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi)
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      mean(abs(comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi))
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      sqrt(mean((comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi)^2))
    ),
    scales::percent(
      mean(abs(comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi) <= 0.10),
      accuracy = 0.1
    )
  )
)

kable(
  hsi_comparison,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "r")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-hsi-comparison
#| fig-cap: "Spatial comparison of MaxEnt and HSI habitat-suitability predictions. Positive differences indicate greater suitability predicted by MaxEnt."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

suitability_difference <- maxent_suitability - hsi_suitability

difference_limit <- max(
  abs(range(getValues(suitability_difference), na.rm = TRUE))
)

old_par <- par(
  mfrow = c(1, 3),
  mar = c(2, 2, 3, 5)
)

raster::plot(
  maxent_suitability,
  col = hcl.colors(100, "YlGn"),
  zlim = c(0, 1),
  main = "MaxEnt",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

raster::plot(
  hsi_suitability,
  col = hcl.colors(100, "YlGn"),
  zlim = c(0, 1),
  main = "HSI",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

raster::plot(
  suitability_difference,
  col = hcl.colors(100, "Blue-Red 3"),
  zlim = c(-difference_limit, difference_limit),
  main = "MaxEnt minus HSI",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

par(old_par)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-hsi-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Cell-level relationship between MaxEnt and HSI habitat-suitability predictions. The dashed line represents perfect agreement."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

set.seed(42)

comparison_plot_data <- comparison_data %>%
  slice_sample(n = min(20000, n()))

ggplot(
  comparison_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = hsi,
    y = maxent
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    color = "#2166AC",
    alpha = 0.15,
    size = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey30"
  ) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "HSI suitability",
    y = "MaxEnt suitability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Writing outline: Summary of Major Results

2. Four water-quality surfaces: power 0.25 and range 10 km, with repeated MAE of 0.431 mg/L for oxygen, 2.490 ppt for salinity, 0.745 NTU for turbidity, and 0.988 degrees C for temperature.
3. Selected MaxEnt: LQH with regularization multiplier 0.5, using 34 presences and 10,000 background points. Mean four-partition AUC was 0.703 (SD 0.136) and omission was 11.46% (SD 9.10 percentage points).
4. The saved logistic suitability surface covered 324.55 square km, with mean relative suitability 0.236. Across 317.74 square km shared with the HSI, exact agreement was 27.54%, agreement within one class was 73.38%, and Spearman rho was 0.273.
